concept.body: Read a congruence statement like a two-row table: write ABC above DEF and draw three vertical lines. A pairs with D, B with E, C with F. Any part's partner is found by swapping each letter for the one directly below it.

explanationVariants: Under ΔJKL ≅ ΔXYZ the columns are J|X, K|Y, L|Z, so ∠K's partner is ∠Y.
K is the middle letter; the middle letter of XYZ is Y.

widget.prompt: ΔJKL ≅ ΔXYZ. Which angle corresponds to ∠K?

options.label: ∠Y
options.feedback: Middle letter pairs with middle letter: K↔Y.

options.label: ∠X
options.feedback: X is the FIRST letter — that's J's partner. K sits in the middle, above Y.

options.label: ∠Z
options.feedback: Z is the THIRD letter — L's partner. K's column holds Y.

options.label: ∠L
options.feedback: L is K's neighbor in the SAME triangle — partners live across the ≅ sign, in the matching column.

steps.body: A congruence statement is a **cipher**. In ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF the letter ORDER carries the correspondence: A↔D, B↔E, C↔F — first with first, second with second, third with third. From it, matched parts read off by POSITION: AB ≅ DE, BC ≅ EF, ∠C ≅ ∠F. Never trust the picture; trust the order.

widget.prompt: ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF. Match each part of ΔABC with its corresponding part of ΔDEF.

pairErrors.feedback: AB uses letters in positions 1–2, so its partner uses positions 1–2 of DEF: DE. EF is the 2–3 side — BC's partner.
∠A is the FIRST letter, so its partner is the first letter of DEF: ∠D. ∠F pairs with the third letter, ∠C.
BC sits in positions 2–3, so its partner is EF. DE is the 1–2 side, already claimed by AB.

widget.missFeedback: Match by POSITION in the statement: 1st↔1st, 2nd↔2nd, 3rd↔3rd.

explanationVariants: H and J are the 2nd and 3rd letters of GHJ, so HJ pairs with the 2nd and 3rd letters of PQR: QR.
Map letter by letter — G↔P, H↔Q, J↔R — then translate HJ through the map: QR.

widget.prompt: ΔGHJ ≅ ΔPQR. Which segment is congruent to HJ?

options.label: QR
options.feedback: Positions 2–3 on both sides: H↔Q and J↔R, so HJ ≅ QR.

options.label: PQ
options.feedback: PQ occupies positions 1–2 — that's GH's partner. HJ lives in positions 2–3: QR.

options.label: PR
options.feedback: PR spans positions 1–3, partnering GJ. HJ's slots are 2–3: QR.

options.label: GJ
options.feedback: GJ is a side of the SAME triangle as HJ — correspondence pairs parts ACROSS the two triangles.

steps.body: The cipher also moves **numbers**. Since corresponding parts of congruent figures are congruent, a measurement known on one triangle teleports to its positional partner on the other — and ONLY to its partner. The commonest slip: grabbing a measurement from the matching-looking side instead of the matching-POSITION side.

explanationVariants: DE partners AB (positions 1–2), so DE = AB = 9. The 12 belongs to EF, whose partner is BC.
Translate DE backward through the cipher: D↔A, E↔B, so DE ≅ AB = 9.

widget.prompt: ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF, with AB = 9, EF = 12, and m∠A = 40°. Find DE.

commonErrors.feedback: 12 is EF — but EF (positions 2–3) partners BC, not DE. DE sits in positions 1–2, partnering AB = 9.
40° is an ANGLE measure (∠A's). DE is a side — its positional partner is AB, so DE = 9.

explanationVariants: ∠F is the third letter; its partner is the third letter ∠C, so m∠F = 64°.
C↔F under the cipher — the measure carries across unchanged (rigid motions preserve angles).

widget.prompt: ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF and m∠C = 64°. Find m∠F in degrees.

commonErrors.feedback: 26 is the COMPLEMENT (90 − 64). Complements come from right-angle pairs — correspondence copies the measure as-is: 64°.
116 is the SUPPLEMENT (180 − 64). No straight line is involved — ∠F simply inherits its partner's measure: 64°.

steps.body: Statements can be **rewritten** — but every rewrite must respect the same point pairing. If ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF, then listing the first triangle as ΔBCA forces the second into ΔEFD: each letter drags its partner to the same new position. Same fact, new outfit.

widget.prompt: Given ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF, complete the rewrite: ΔBCA ≅ Δ___

options.label: EFD
options.feedback: B↔E, C↔F, A↔D — reorder the left side and each partner follows to the same slot: EFD.

options.label: DEF
options.feedback: Keeping DEF while reordering to BCA breaks the pairing: it would match B with D, but B's partner is E. Partners must move together.

options.label: FDE
options.feedback: FDE pairs B↔F — but F belongs to C. Push each of B, C, A through the original map: E, F, D.

options.label: DFE
options.feedback: DFE matches C with F correctly but swaps the other two: it pairs B↔D and A↔E, reversing the true B↔E, A↔D.

hints: Write the original pairing first: A↔?, B↔?, C↔?.
A↔D, B↔E, C↔F. Now push C, A, B through it, in that order.
C goes to F, A goes to D, B goes to E — assemble the letters.
explanationVariants: Push each letter of CAB through the map A↔D, B↔E, C↔F: C→F, A→D, B→E, giving ΔFDE.
The rewrite test: same pairs, new order. ΔCAB ≅ ΔFDE keeps every original partnership intact.

widget.prompt: Given ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF, complete: ΔCAB ≅ Δ___

options.label: FDE
options.feedback: C→F, A→D, B→E — each letter's original partner, in the new order.

options.label: DEF
options.feedback: DEF pairs C↔D — but C's partner is F. The right side must reorder along WITH the left: FDE.

options.label: EFD
options.feedback: EFD is the partner of ΔBCA (B→E, C→F, A→D). Here the left side starts with C, so the right must start with C's partner, F.

options.label: FED
options.feedback: FED starts right (C↔F) but then pairs A↔E and B↔D — swapping the last two partnerships. A's partner is D: FDE.

takeaways: Letter order encodes the pairing: 1st↔1st, 2nd↔2nd, 3rd↔3rd — trust it over any picture.
Measurements teleport only between POSITIONAL partners.
Rewrites must drag partners to matching slots: ΔCAB ≅ ΔFDE.
steps.teaser: Course complete! Next course: constructions with compass and straightedge — and your first real proofs.
